title: Optional structured Failure model
summary: Normative portable Failure payload model that remains optional inside the unconstrained generic Result failure channel.

result_compatibility: Result<T,E> and Err<E> continue to accept every previously valid E
Failure is selected explicitly as an error payload by writing Err<Failure>
FailureData<E> remains the canonical name of the ResultData failure branch and is not redefined
No automatic coercion from arbitrary E, exception, HTTP response, or RPC status is permitted

fields.semantics: Selects decoding and compatibility rules for the portable payload.
Stable machine identity owned by its URI namespace rather than presentation text.
Fallback presentation only; never identity and never an authorization input.
Localization lookup key that does not change failure identity.
Public-safe localization arguments with JSON-only values.
Domain detail whose interpretation is governed by code ownership.
Direct causes in deterministic order; cycles are forbidden.
Operational hints that never replace code or define transport mappings implicitly.
Public portable metadata subject to boundary redaction policy.
Namespaced extension bag; unknown top-level fields remain forbidden.

code_policy: Code MUST be an absolute RFC 3986 URI and MUST NOT depend on localized presentation
The URI namespace owner governs code meaning and detail schema without a global hardcoded registry
HTTP status, RPC status, exception class, and UI copy MUST NOT be inferred unless an explicit adapter maps the code
version_policy: Major version changes may remove fields or alter field semantics and require explicit migration
Minor-compatible readers ignore only namespaced extension keys and reject unknown top-level fields
A reader MUST reject an unsupported major version rather than silently reinterpret the payload
cause_policy: Causes are ordered direct causes and may represent one causal predecessor or an aggregate
Cause graphs MUST be acyclic and bounded by a selected resource profile
Runtime exception objects and stack traces are diagnostic sidecars and MUST NOT appear in portable causes
security_policy: Message, message arguments, details, metadata, and extensions are public-boundary data unless a stricter profile rejects them
Secrets, credentials, stack traces, process paths, and raw exception objects MUST NOT be serialized into portable Failure
Redaction MUST preserve schema_version and code so identity survives presentation removal
Validators MUST bound depth, direct cause count, and total traversed nodes before accepting untrusted input
Failure code and classification MUST NOT independently authorize retries, disclosure, access, or tenant selection

projections.binding: Failure type and Failure(input, limits) constructor with isFailure guard
Frozen Failure dataclass and explicit to_failure_data mapping
Optional structured-failure relation group; generic Result storage remains unchanged
Explicit optional profile with STRICT tables and no reverse authority
No mutation; admission and stricter boundary mapping require external authority
